settings.analytics_help: Choose which usage statistics to share with the developer through PostHog. Sharing starts only after you allow each category. Your documents, filenames, questions and answers are never included. Save settings to apply your choice.
settings.analytics_usage_help: A random installation ID, first consented launch and app openings.
settings.analytics_product_help: Counts of projects, saved cards and exports, plus export format and a random installation ID. No content is shared.
consent.title: Help improve Ankigen?
consent.description: May we send installation, activity and creation counts to PostHog? No documents or card content are shared. You can choose the categories below or change them later in Settings.
settings.analytics_details: Events include a random installation ID, event ID, time, app version, operating system family, counts and export format. There are no screen recordings or user profiles. Location enrichment is disabled; PostHog still receives your IP address as part of the connection. Usage is visible in the developer's private dashboard.
settings.analytics_withdrawal: You can turn this off and save at any time. Pending events are removed; a request already in progress may finish. Events already received remain under the dashboard's retention policy. The random ID stays on this device so enabling statistics again does not count as another installation. Offline events are kept for up to 7 days, with a maximum of 500 events.

help.anki_header: The separator, the HTML flag and the deck column are already declared in the file header — you should not have to change the import settings.
help.anki_import: In Anki: File > Import, pick the .tsv file.
help.anki_media: If your cards use images, copy everything in the export's media/ folder into your Anki profile's collection.media folder, with Anki closed. The "Copy media into Anki" button does this for you.
help.intro: Ankigen turns a structured .docx course into an Anki deck, with you and Claude in the loop — it never invents cards on its own.
help.skill_intro: A skill is a folder holding a SKILL.md file: YAML frontmatter with a name and a description saying when to use it, then the instructions in Markdown. Claude loads it when the task matches, so you never paste the same instructions twice.
help.skill_location: Put it in your Claude skills folder, one folder per skill, then start a conversation and send it a chunk.
help.skill_template_help: Copy this into a SKILL.md file. It is a working starting point, not a rulebook — the HTML colour conventions are one person's habits, but the output format and the image/table placeholders are what Ankigen actually reads at export time.
help.step_chunks: Ankigen splits the document into chunks, one per section, and derives an Anki deck path from the heading hierarchy.
help.step_claude: Copy a chunk and send it to Claude, which has your card-writing skill loaded.
help.step_export: Export as TSV, or as ZIP when your cards use images.
help.step_paste: Paste Claude's tab-separated answer back, check the card preview, save, move to the next chunk.
help.step_upload: Import a .docx whose headings use real heading styles — that is what the splitting relies on.

timeline.err.precision_invalid: “{value}” is not a precision. Accepted values: day, month, year, decade, century, millennium.

timeline.norm.year_as_number: Year written as a number, converted to text.
timeline.norm.trimmed: Spaces at the start or end removed.
timeline.norm.whitespace_collapsed: Repeated spaces or line breaks replaced by a single space.
timeline.hint.json_invalid: Return strict JSON: double quotes around every key and string, commas between items, nothing after the closing brace.
timeline.hint.json_trailing_comma: Remove the comma before the closing bracket or brace.
timeline.hint.json_smart_quotes: Use straight double quotes (") instead of typographic quotes.
timeline.hint.key_unknown: Remove this key: only the keys of the format are accepted.
timeline.hint.id_invalid: Lowercase letters, digits, “_” and “-” only, starting with a letter or a digit, 48 characters at most.
timeline.hint.date_invalid: Accepted forms: "1971", "1971-08", "1971-08-15", and "-44" for 44 BC. For an approximate date, write the year and add "approx": true.
timeline.hint.date_year_zero: 1 BC ("-1") is directly followed by AD 1 ("1").
timeline.hint.precision_mismatch: Leave "precision" out to derive it from the date. "decade", "century" and "millennium" take a year alone: a round year for a decade ("1970"), the first year for a century ("1501").
timeline.hint.present_not_allowed: For an ongoing period, write the start date in "start" and "present" in "end".
timeline.hint.end_before_start: Swap the two dates, or check the BC dates: "-509" comes before "-27".
timeline.hint.eras_overlap: Eras are successive backgrounds: make each one start where the previous one ends.
timeline.hint.century_ambiguous: Write the first year of the century: "1501" for the 16th century.
timeline.hint.millennium_ambiguous: Write the first year of the millennium: "2001" for the 3rd millennium.
timeline.hint.label_contains_year: Remove the year from the label.
